clue.text: Some in theatre know Long Day's Journey into Night, say

definitions.text: Long Day's Journey into Night, say

indicators.note: only some of the letters inside the words theatre know are taken, a run spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Part of a theatre audience is familiar with O'Neill's play Long Day's Journey into Night.
explanation.walkthrough: The play title pretends to be literary, but it is just an example of a long, hard journey; 'say' flags the example.
explanation.definitionFit: A long and arduous journey, like one lasting from day into night, is an arduous expedition on foot.

clue.text: Two things to do with camera in volatile situation

parts.words: Two things to do with camera
parts.note: a camera has a flash, one thing it does

parts.words: Two things to do with camera
parts.note: you point a camera, the other thing you do with it

explanation.surface: A photographer finds themselves snapping a tense, explosive scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the moment or place where tension erupts into violence or crisis.

clue.text: Arresting picture's warning to cocoa drinker?

definitions.meaning: a photograph taken by police on arrest
read as '...', a caution that the cup is scalding

explanation.walkthrough: 'Arresting' sounds like 'striking' but means made at an arrest; the second reading splits the word into a little sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A police photo of a suspect's face, taken when they are booked after being arrested.

clue.text: Wide edge taken off machete, a big one

parts.note: W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide

indicators.note: the first letter, the edge of the synonym for machete, is removed

parts.note: a machete is a chopper, a big cutting blade

explanation.surface: A wide machete has been blunted along its edge, and it was a big one.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a wide is a ball bowled out of the batter's reach, scored as W.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: something unusually large, a whacking great example (also a big lie).

clue.text: Breaking placard, mother grabbing attention against faction's dirty tricks

indicators.note: the other pieces break into the word for placard, splitting it apart

parts.note: a placard is a sign

indicators.note: the word for mother grabs, that is holds inside it, the next pieces

parts.note: MA is a familiar word for mother

indicators.note: against here means placed next to, the two pieces side by side

parts.note: to have someone's ear is to have their attention
a camp is a faction or group within a party

explanation.surface: Protesters break a placard while a mother tries to get attention, in a story of one faction's underhand tactics.
explanation.definitionFit: A coordinated effort to damage a rival's reputation is a form of political dirty tricks.

clue.text: Fire exit

definitions.meaning: a gun or alarm fires when it is set off

explanation.definitionFit: A gun can discharge, as a gun discharges; and to leave a place is to depart from it.

clue.text: Queen consort popular always among half of visitors

indicators.note: the next pieces go among, so inside, the letters from visitors
only half the synonym for visitors is kept, its last three letters cut

parts.note: visitors are guests
IN means popular or fashionable
ever means always

explanation.surface: A royal wife is popular with half her guests at all times.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthurian legend: King Arthur's wife, a royal consort famed for her affair with Lancelot.

clue.text: Longhair waving at a garçon

indicators.note: waving moves the letters of at a garcon about into a new order

explanation.surface: A long-haired man waves at a waiter in a French cafe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Longhair' suggests a hippie or highbrow; it is a long-haired breed of cat. The cedilla on the c is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a breed of cat with long silky fur, described by owners as a longhair.

clue.text: End of laser beam's missing subsequently

indicators.note: the final letter of laser is missing from the synonym for beam

parts.note: a rafter is a roof beam; the 's stands for is

indicators.note: the end of the word laser is its last letter

explanation.surface: The tip of a laser beam has gone astray afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laser beam' looks like one thing, but beam is a roof timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: later on, following something in time.

clue.text: Disobeying orders aboard sinking boat, men worried about commotion

parts.note: aboard means in, on board
a sub (submarine) is a boat built to submerge
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers
din is noisy commotion
what's eating you means what is worrying you, so worried is ate

explanation.surface: Men on a submarine going down panic over the uproar and refuse their orders.
explanation.walkthrough: OR (other ranks) is a crossword staple for men; 'about' links ATE (worried) to the din it is worried about.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: rebellious, refusing to obey those in authority.

clue.text: Concerned with nitrogen in adulterated Asti wine

parts.note: RE means about or concerning, as in letters

indicators.note: the symbol for nitrogen goes inside the rearranged letters
adulterated means tampered with, so the letters of Asti are mixed

parts.note: N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: Someone worries about nitrogen in a spiked Italian sparkling wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adulterated' makes TSIA from ASTI, and 'in' puts N into it before the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a Greek white or rosé wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: Soft Communist embracing European Trot's conclusion

indicators.note: the Soviet leader's name embraces, holds inside, the abbreviation for European

parts.note: Lenin, the Russian communist leader

indicators.note: the conclusion of Trot's is its last letter

explanation.surface: A Communist leader embraces a European Trotskyist at the end of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trot' suggests Trotsky alongside Lenin, but only its final letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: mild, tolerant, not harsh in punishment.

clue.text: Give period of light current

parts.note: to present something is to give it
day is the period of daylight between night and night

explanation.surface: An electrician hands over a daytime spell of electrical current.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light current' suggests electricity; current is the definition, meaning of now.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: belonging to the present time, contemporary.

clue.text: Small isolated place did trifle, mostly sent back

indicators.note: the shortened word is sent back, read from right to left
mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: to trifle with is to toy with, so did trifle is toyed

explanation.surface: Someone at a remote spot played about with things, then returned most of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the D of TOYED, and 'sent back' turns TOYE round.
explanation.definitionFit: A small island, especially one in a river such as the Thames, is an isolated spot.

clue.text: What could make you slim, eating pips?

indicators.note: the answer could be rearranged to make the words slim eating, which signals mixing those letters

explanation.surface: Someone asks what diet would slim them down if they eat fruit pips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pips' looks like fruit seeds; it is the BBC radio's six short beeps marking the hour, the Greenwich pips.
explanation.definitionFit: British radio: the pips are the hourly beeps broadcast to mark exact time.

clue.text: English composer dismissing a conservationist Spanish artist

indicators.note: the composer's name dismisses, drops, the letter a

parts.note: Edward Elgar, English composer of the Enigma Variations
ECO is short for an ecologist or conservationist

explanation.surface: An English composer sacks a conservationist in favour of a Spanish painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Domenikos Theotokopoulos, the Cretan-born painter of Toledo known by his Spanish nickname.

clue.text: Not inclined to move, teach girl dancing

indicators.note: dancing moves the letters of teach girl about into a new order

explanation.surface: A sluggish pupil who won't budge: teach the girl to dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: sluggish and drowsy, lacking energy to do anything.

clue.text: Make sure of winning patch?

definitions.meaning: to clinch or secure a result

explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to secure victory beyond doubt; literally, to stitch up a hole as a repair.

clue.text: Great number for living allowance

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
life is living
a ration is a fixed allowance

explanation.surface: A large sum paid out as a living allowance.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapid multiplication, and so a large quantity of something.

clue.text: Mischief-maker and unclothed vocalist make an impression

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous little devil

indicators.note: unclothed strips the outer letters, the clothes, from the word for vocalist

parts.note: a vocalist is a singer

explanation.surface: A prankster and a naked singer certainly make their mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To have an effect on, encroach upon, leaving a mark on something.

clue.text: Fine furrow over top of field

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the word goes upwards, reading it backwards

parts.note: a rut is a furrow or groove
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A fine furrow runs across the top of a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top of field' looks like a first-letter pick but is the definition: the grassy surface layer.
explanation.definitionFit: The top layer of grass and roots covering a field is sod.

clue.text: Silence in this place benefiting poor part of England

parts.note: here means this place
for means benefiting, on behalf of

indicators.note: the call for silence goes in among the other pieces

parts.note: dire means very poor
SH is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A call for quiet in a deprived area of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silence in this place' reads as one phrase, but 'in' is the container signal. This West Midlands county on the Welsh border is famed for its cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a county on the Welsh border, a region of England.

clue.text: Songbird is to tolerate insecticide with drug in it

parts.note: to bear is to tolerate

indicators.note: the drug letter goes inside the insecticide's abbreviation

parts.note: DDT, the banned insecticide
E is ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: A songbird can put up with pesticide that has drugs in it.
explanation.walkthrough: E goes after the first D of DDT, making DEDT.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a reedbed bird with black facial markings, also called the bearded reedling.

clue.text: Bury article, getting up to trouble with others

parts.note: to inter is to bury
A is the indefinite article

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means the word rises, read bottom to top

parts.note: to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: Bury an item, then get up to mischief with others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting up to trouble' reads as making mischief; 'getting up' reverses AIL to LIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin phrase meaning among other things, used for things alongside others.

clue.text: It's tough to eat leg: stir vigorously

indicators.note: vigorously suggests the letters of leg and stir being stirred hard into a new order

explanation.surface: A cook stirs a leg of meat hard because it's tough to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Tough cartilage in meat that is hard to chew.

clue.text: Attempt to cover grey that doesn't end well?

indicators.note: the word for attempt covers, encloses, the word for grey

parts.note: a try is an attempt
grey means old, aged

explanation.surface: Trying to dye grey hair ends badly.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama or event ending in disaster, the opposite of a happy ending.

clue.text: Fine example of Scottish isle mentioned

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken, so the word sounds like the island's name

parts.note: Bute is an island in the Firth of Clyde

explanation.surface: A Scottish island is talked about as an excellent specimen.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: a beauty, an outstanding specimen of something.

clue.text: Produce credit on work

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Agricultural produce is credited on the farm's work.
explanation.definitionFit: A harvest of grown produce from the fields.
